jsonld.description: Technology cost structure analysis tool for PE diligence and portfolio company benchmarking
header.subtitle: Benchmark total technology cost against stage-adjusted ranges. Built for IC packages, board reporting, and sell-side preparation.
onboarding.p1: TechPar benchmarks your total technology cost against stage-adjusted ranges derived from KeyBanc, OpenView, Bessemer, and GST engagement data.
onboarding.p2: Who it's for: PE deal teams, portfolio company CTOs and CFOs, and board-level reporting.
onboarding.p3: What you'll need: Annual recurring revenue (ARR) and monthly infrastructure spend at minimum. Additional cost categories (personnel, R&D, CapEx) unlock deeper analysis.
onboarding.p4: How it works: Select your company stage, enter revenue and costs, and TechPar computes a blended technology cost ratio with zone classification, gap analysis, and 36-month trajectory projection.

analysis.title: Analysis
analysis.sub: Technology cost structure benchmarked against stage-adjusted ranges.
analysis.emptyMsg:
Enter ARR on the Profile tab
to compute TechPar.
analysis.heroLabel: total technology cost as % of revenue
bench.sources: Ranges informed by KeyBanc SaaS Survey (2024), OpenView Benchmarks (2024), Bessemer State of the Cloud (2024), and GST engagement experience (2023–2025). Benchmarks are reviewed annually. Individual results vary based on business model and organizational structure.
bench.industryDisclaimer: These benchmarks are derived primarily from SaaS company data. Companies operating marketplace, fintech, infrastructure, or hardware-intensive models may observe materially different cost structures. Apply professional judgment when benchmarking outside a pure-SaaS context.
methodology.sources.heading: Benchmark sources
methodology.sources.body: Ranges are informed by KeyBanc SaaS Survey (2024), OpenView Benchmarks (2024), Bessemer State of the Cloud (2024), and calibrated against GST engagement experience (2023–2025). Benchmarks are reviewed annually and represent the interquartile range of technology cost as a percentage of revenue at each growth stage.
methodology.zones.heading: Zone threshold derivation
methodology.zones.body: Each company stage defines five thresholds that partition spend into six zones. The healthy range (low/high) represents the benchmark interquartile range. Below that, an underinvestment floor flags spend levels that may constrain engineering velocity or platform reliability. Above the healthy ceiling, the above-par, elevated, and critical thresholds flag increasingly significant cost drag. Thresholds are stage-specific: early-stage companies carry higher healthy ranges (60–100% at Seed) than mature companies (18–32% at Enterprise).
methodology.gap.heading: Gap calculation
methodology.gap.body: The 36-month cumulative excess is computed by projecting monthly revenue forward at your stated growth rate, then summing the difference between your technology cost ratio and the stage ceiling in each month where spend exceeds the ceiling. For PE-backed and Enterprise stages, this excess is multiplied by the exit multiple to estimate the implied impact on recoverable exit value.
methodology.trajectory.heading: Trajectory projections
methodology.trajectory.body: The trajectory chart projects a constant technology cost ratio against growing revenue over 36 months. It assumes costs scale linearly with revenue at the current ratio. Actual trajectory depends on optimization decisions, scaling dynamics, and organizational changes not captured in this model.
methodology.limits.heading: Limitations
methodology.limits.body: TechPar provides a directional benchmark, not a precise diagnostic. It does not account for one-time costs, migration expenses, or business-model-specific factors. Category benchmarks assume a SaaS-oriented cost structure. Results should be interpreted alongside qualitative context and validated against company-specific circumstances.

js.metrics.trajNote.seed: At Seed / Pre-A, trajectory matters more than the current number. The key question is whether this ratio declines as revenue scales.
js.metrics.trajNote.series_a: At Series A, trajectory matters more than the current number. The key question is whether this ratio declines as revenue scales.
js.metrics.trajNote.series_bc: At Series B–C, trajectory matters more than the current number. The key question is whether this ratio declines as revenue scales.
stage.seed.note: At seed stage, a high technology cost ratio is expected. Infrastructure often leads revenue. What matters is whether the ratio trends down as ARR scales.
stage.seed.noteUnder: At seed stage, technology spend below 15% of ARR may indicate underinvestment in core infrastructure or product. Ensure critical systems are adequately resourced before optimising for efficiency.
stage.series_a.note: Series A companies often carry cost structures from rapid early growth. The key question is whether technology spend as a percentage of revenue is declining as you scale.
stage.series_a.noteUnder: Technology spend below 12% of ARR at Series A may signal underinvestment in engineering or infrastructure. Sustained underspend can impair product velocity and create technical debt that is costly to unwind later.
stage.series_bc.note: At Series B–C, technology spend should be converging toward a sustainable ratio. Persistent overspend signals architectural issues that compound as you scale toward profitability.
stage.series_bc.noteUnder: Technology spend below 10% of ARR at Series B–C is atypically lean. Verify that engineering capacity and infrastructure are sufficient to support your growth targets before attributing this to efficiency.
stage.pe.note: In a PE context, every percentage point above the 40% ceiling translates directly to EBITDA compression and exit value. Technology cost optimization is a financial engineering lever.
stage.pe.noteUnder: Technology spend below 8% of ARR in a PE-backed company warrants scrutiny. Underinvestment in infrastructure or engineering capacity can suppress growth and create execution risk at exit.
stage.enterprise.note: At enterprise scale, technology spend as a percentage of revenue is typically well below early-stage norms. Persistent spend above 32% warrants a structural review.
stage.enterprise.noteUnder: Technology spend below 6% of ARR at enterprise scale can indicate underinvestment in modernisation or maintenance. Legacy system risk and engineering capacity constraints often surface as operational drag over time.
signal.seed.underinvest.headline: Possible underinvestment.
signal.seed.underinvest.body: Very lean technology spend at seed stage can constrain engineering velocity, product reliability, and the ability to scale when growth accelerates.
signal.seed.ahead.headline: Efficient for seed stage.
signal.seed.ahead.body: Below the healthy band. Strong margin profile, though watch for reliability and velocity constraints as you push for growth.
signal.seed.healthy.headline: Normal for this stage.
signal.seed.healthy.body: Technology spend is within the expected range for a pre-Series A company. Focus on architecture that scales as revenue grows.
signal.seed.above.headline: High, but not uncommon.
signal.seed.above.body: Above the upper range, though seed-stage investment ahead of revenue is expected. Monitor whether the ratio converges as ARR grows.
signal.seed.elevated.headline: Watch the trajectory.
signal.seed.elevated.body: Significantly above range. Not alarming if revenue is scaling fast. The ratio should decline quarter over quarter.
signal.seed.critical.headline: Technology drag at seed stage.
signal.seed.critical.body: This level of spend relative to early revenue warrants a structural review of engineering efficiency and architecture choices.
signal.series_a.underinvest.headline: Possible underinvestment.
signal.series_a.underinvest.body: Engineering velocity, platform reliability, and scaling capacity may be constrained. Examine whether technology spend aligns with roadmap ambition.
signal.series_a.ahead.headline: Efficient for Series A.
signal.series_a.ahead.body: Below the healthy band. Strong margin position, provided product reliability and scaling capacity are not being compromised.
signal.series_a.healthy.headline: Within healthy range.
signal.series_a.healthy.body: Spend is well-calibrated for a Series A company. As ARR scales, this ratio should continue to improve without active intervention.
signal.series_a.above.headline: Above benchmark. Watch the trend.
signal.series_a.above.body: Above the healthy range but not unusual for a scaling company. The concern is whether the ratio is improving as revenue grows.
signal.series_a.elevated.headline: Elevated. Convergence expected.
signal.series_a.elevated.body: Persistently high technology spend at this stage often signals architectural inefficiency. If the ratio is not declining with revenue growth, structural work may be needed.
signal.series_a.critical.headline: Structural review warranted.
signal.series_a.critical.body: At this level, technology spend is a meaningful drag on the path to profitability. An architectural and operational review should be prioritized.
signal.series_bc.underinvest.headline: Below minimum threshold.
signal.series_bc.underinvest.body: Low technology spend may constrain platform scalability and reliability. Deferred investment at this stage often surfaces as production incidents at scale.
signal.series_bc.ahead.headline: Technology cost advantage.
signal.series_bc.ahead.body: Running lean relative to benchmark. Ensure this reflects genuine efficiency rather than deferred reliability or scalability investment.
signal.series_bc.healthy.headline: Well-calibrated for this stage.
signal.series_bc.healthy.body: Spend sits inside the healthy range. Maintain discipline as headcount and engineering complexity scale.
signal.series_bc.above.headline: Above benchmark. Opportunity to optimize.
signal.series_bc.above.body: The window to address structural inefficiency is now, before the cost baseline sets at scale.
signal.series_bc.elevated.headline: Value creation risk.
signal.series_bc.elevated.body: Persistently elevated spend at this stage will compound toward exit. Architectural inefficiency that is addressable now becomes expensive technical debt later.
signal.series_bc.critical.headline: Material drag on the path to profitability.
signal.series_bc.critical.body: Technology at this percentage is a significant obstacle to the EBITDA profile that drives Series B–C valuations.
signal.pe.underinvest.headline: Below minimum threshold.
signal.pe.underinvest.body: While efficient, this level may indicate deferred investment that will surface as reliability risk or technical debt in a sell-side process.
signal.pe.ahead.headline: Efficient. Margin advantage.
signal.pe.ahead.body: Technology spend is below the benchmark range, contributing positively to EBITDA. Verify this reflects genuine optimization and not deferred investment.
signal.pe.healthy.headline: Within benchmark range.
signal.pe.healthy.body: Spend supports a clean technology narrative in any sell-side or IC process.
signal.pe.above.headline: Above benchmark. Quantifiable impact.
signal.pe.above.body: Every point above 40% reduces EBITDA directly. The cumulative drag over a hold period, and its exit value translation, are significant.
signal.pe.elevated.headline: Value creation priority.
signal.pe.elevated.body: Technology optimization is among the highest-return value creation initiatives available. The dollar impact compounds across the hold period.
signal.pe.critical.headline: Material exit value drag.
signal.pe.critical.body: Technology at this percentage is a significant detractor in any valuation model. This needs to be addressed as a financial priority.
signal.enterprise.underinvest.headline: Below minimum threshold.
signal.enterprise.underinvest.body: At enterprise scale this may reflect aggressive cost reduction with implications for platform reliability, SLA delivery, and roadmap execution capacity.
signal.enterprise.ahead.headline: Strong technology efficiency.
signal.enterprise.ahead.body: Running well below the healthy range. Healthy at enterprise scale, provided this reflects genuine efficiency and not infrastructure debt accumulation.
signal.enterprise.healthy.headline: Within healthy range for enterprise.
signal.enterprise.healthy.body: Spend is well-calibrated. Technology efficiency at this level supports strong EBITDA margins.
signal.enterprise.above.headline: Above enterprise benchmark.
signal.enterprise.above.body: Likely reflects legacy architecture, multi-cloud complexity, or deferred rationalization work.
signal.enterprise.elevated.headline: Structural review warranted.
signal.enterprise.elevated.body: Technology spend represents a meaningful EBITDA drag relative to enterprise peers. A rationalization roadmap should be a near-term priority.
signal.enterprise.critical.headline: Significant efficiency gap.
signal.enterprise.critical.body: Technology at this percentage is an outlier for enterprise scale. A structural review of architecture, vendor contracts, and operational practices is overdue.
rec.seed.underinvest.1: Ensure core infrastructure (CI/CD, monitoring, incident response) is resourced before optimising for cost efficiency.
rec.seed.underinvest.2: Validate that engineering velocity is not being constrained by tooling or platform limitations.
rec.seed.ahead.1: Monitor platform reliability metrics to confirm this efficiency is genuine, not deferred investment.
rec.seed.ahead.2: Document current architecture decisions so the next engineering hire can onboard quickly.
rec.seed.healthy.1: Maintain current discipline as the team grows. Set cost alerts on cloud accounts to catch drift early.
rec.seed.healthy.2: Invest in automated testing and deployment pipelines now to avoid velocity bottlenecks at Series A.
rec.seed.above.1: Review cloud resource utilisation: identify idle instances, oversized databases, and unused storage.
rec.seed.above.2: Evaluate whether current tooling subscriptions are still justified at current team size.
rec.seed.above.3: Consider reserved instances or committed use discounts for predictable workloads.
rec.seed.elevated.1: Audit cloud architecture for over-provisioned resources and consolidate redundant services.
rec.seed.elevated.2: Review vendor contracts for renegotiation or consolidation opportunities.
rec.seed.elevated.3: Assess whether any R&D spend is compensating for architectural shortcuts that should be addressed directly.
rec.seed.critical.1: Commission a technology cost audit focused on the three largest spend categories.
rec.seed.critical.2: Evaluate build-vs-buy decisions for non-core platform services.
rec.seed.critical.3: Review team structure for role overlap or misaligned resourcing between infrastructure and product engineering.
rec.series_a.underinvest.1: Assess whether engineering capacity is sufficient to execute on the product roadmap at scale.
rec.series_a.underinvest.2: Validate that infrastructure can handle projected user growth without emergency spend.
rec.series_a.ahead.1: Ensure platform reliability SLAs are being met. Low spend should not come at the cost of uptime.
rec.series_a.ahead.2: Confirm that engineering tooling is not creating velocity bottlenecks masked by low headcount costs.
rec.series_a.healthy.1: Establish cost-per-customer or cost-per-transaction metrics to track efficiency as you scale.
rec.series_a.healthy.2: Set quarterly review cadence for cloud costs to catch drift before it becomes structural.
rec.series_a.above.1: Implement cloud cost tagging by team and service to identify the largest contributors.
rec.series_a.above.2: Review engineering tooling subscriptions for overlapping capabilities.
rec.series_a.above.3: Evaluate whether contractor or outsourced engineering is cost-effective relative to full-time hires.
rec.series_a.elevated.1: Prioritise cloud cost optimisation: reserved instances, right-sizing, and storage tiering.
rec.series_a.elevated.2: Audit R&D tooling for consolidation: CI/CD, monitoring, project management, and communication platforms.
rec.series_a.elevated.3: Review engineering team structure for alignment between headcount and roadmap priorities.
rec.series_a.critical.1: Engage a cloud cost optimisation partner or conduct a formal technology spend audit.
rec.series_a.critical.2: Evaluate architectural decisions that may be driving disproportionate infrastructure costs.
rec.series_a.critical.3: Assess whether current engineering headcount is matched to the right projects.
rec.series_bc.underinvest.1: Validate that infrastructure reliability and engineering velocity support your growth targets.
rec.series_bc.underinvest.2: Assess whether deferred technology investment is creating hidden technical debt.
rec.series_bc.ahead.1: Document the practices driving this efficiency so they can be preserved as the organisation scales.
rec.series_bc.ahead.2: Monitor for early signs of reliability or scalability constraints that low spend may be masking.
rec.series_bc.healthy.1: Establish unit economics for technology cost (cost per customer, cost per transaction).
rec.series_bc.healthy.2: Set up automated alerting for cloud cost anomalies and budget overruns.
rec.series_bc.above.1: Implement granular cloud cost allocation by team, product, and environment.
rec.series_bc.above.2: Review reserved instance and committed use discount coverage across all cloud providers.
rec.series_bc.above.3: Audit engineering tooling: consolidate overlapping SaaS subscriptions and renegotiate enterprise agreements.
rec.series_bc.elevated.1: Commission a cloud architecture review focused on cost-driven refactoring opportunities.
rec.series_bc.elevated.2: Evaluate multi-cloud strategy: consolidation to a primary provider often reduces management overhead and unlocks volume discounts.
rec.series_bc.elevated.3: Review engineering team productivity metrics to ensure headcount is translating to output.
rec.series_bc.critical.1: Engage a technology cost optimisation firm to identify structural inefficiencies.
rec.series_bc.critical.2: Prioritise architectural refactoring for the highest-cost services.
rec.series_bc.critical.3: Evaluate vendor contracts for renegotiation, consolidation, or replacement with open-source alternatives.
rec.pe.underinvest.1: Assess reliability and incident frequency. Low spend may be creating execution risk at exit.
rec.pe.underinvest.2: Validate that engineering capacity supports the value creation plan and roadmap commitments.
rec.pe.ahead.1: Document the technology cost story for sell-side materials. This efficiency is a value driver.
rec.pe.ahead.2: Confirm that this position is sustainable and not dependent on deferred maintenance or technical debt.
rec.pe.healthy.1: Maintain cost discipline through the hold period. Establish quarterly cost reviews with portfolio operations.
rec.pe.healthy.2: Benchmark individual cost categories to identify optimisation opportunities within the healthy range.
rec.pe.above.1: Review cloud contracts: reserved instances, committed use discounts, and vendor consolidation opportunities.
rec.pe.above.2: Audit engineering tooling subscriptions for unused seats, overlapping capabilities, and renegotiation leverage.
rec.pe.above.3: Evaluate build-vs-buy decisions for non-core platform services.
rec.pe.elevated.1: Prioritise cloud cost optimisation as a near-term value creation initiative with measurable EBITDA impact.
rec.pe.elevated.2: Assess engineering team structure: ratio of infrastructure to product engineering headcount.
rec.pe.elevated.3: Review vendor agreements for multi-year commitments that can be restructured or consolidated.
rec.pe.critical.1: Engage a technology cost optimisation firm to scope a 90-day cost reduction plan.
rec.pe.critical.2: Evaluate architectural modernisation opportunities that reduce ongoing run-rate costs.
rec.pe.critical.3: Assess whether current engineering leadership has the operational focus to drive cost discipline.
rec.enterprise.underinvest.1: Review infrastructure modernisation backlog. Legacy system maintenance costs tend to accelerate.
rec.enterprise.underinvest.2: Validate that engineering capacity supports both maintenance obligations and strategic initiatives.
rec.enterprise.ahead.1: Ensure this efficiency is not masking deferred modernisation or accumulated technical debt.
rec.enterprise.ahead.2: Document cost management practices as institutional knowledge for the technology leadership team.
rec.enterprise.healthy.1: Establish annual benchmarking cadence against peers to track relative position.
rec.enterprise.healthy.2: Focus optimisation efforts on specific cost categories rather than across-the-board reductions.
rec.enterprise.above.1: Conduct a cloud and vendor contract rationalisation review across all business units.
rec.enterprise.above.2: Evaluate legacy system maintenance costs and assess modernisation ROI.
rec.enterprise.above.3: Review engineering headcount allocation between maintenance, support, and strategic projects.
rec.enterprise.elevated.1: Engage procurement to renegotiate top-10 vendor contracts with a target of 15-20% reduction.
rec.enterprise.elevated.2: Prioritise infrastructure modernisation for services with the highest run-rate costs.
rec.enterprise.elevated.3: Evaluate shared services consolidation across business units or product lines.
rec.enterprise.critical.1: Commission a comprehensive technology rationalisation programme with executive sponsorship.
rec.enterprise.critical.2: Evaluate cloud migration or consolidation strategy for on-premise workloads.
rec.enterprise.critical.3: Assess organisational structure for redundant technology teams across business units.
industry.saas.disclaimer: These benchmarks are derived from SaaS company data and are directly applicable to your business model.
industry.fintech.note: Fintech companies typically carry 10-20% higher infrastructure costs than pure SaaS due to compliance infrastructure, payment processing, and data security requirements. R&D ratios are comparable, but regulatory engineering and audit readiness can drive personnel costs above benchmark. Consider adjusting the healthy range upward by 5-10 percentage points when interpreting results.
industry.fintech.disclaimer: These benchmarks are derived primarily from SaaS company data. Fintech companies typically carry higher infrastructure and compliance costs. Apply professional judgment when interpreting zone classifications.
industry.marketplace.note: Marketplace businesses often show lower technology-to-revenue ratios than SaaS because revenue recognition differs. Technology cost as a percentage of GMV is often a more relevant metric than technology cost as a percentage of net revenue. If you entered net revenue, your ratios may appear healthier than the underlying economics suggest. If you entered GMV, ratios will appear elevated relative to SaaS benchmarks.
industry.marketplace.disclaimer: These benchmarks are derived primarily from SaaS company data. Marketplace revenue recognition differs materially. Consider whether net revenue or GMV is the appropriate denominator for your analysis.
industry.infra_hw.note: Infrastructure and hardware-intensive companies carry cost structures that differ fundamentally from SaaS. Hardware COGS, manufacturing R&D, and embedded software development are not captured in these benchmarks. Software-only technology spend as a percentage of revenue is typically 5-15 percentage points lower than SaaS norms at the same stage. Use these results as a directional reference for the software layer only.
industry.infra_hw.disclaimer: These benchmarks are derived primarily from SaaS company data. Infrastructure and hardware-intensive models have fundamentally different cost structures. Results reflect the software technology layer only.
industry.other.note: Your industry may have cost structures that differ from SaaS benchmarks. Use these results as a directional reference and validate against industry-specific data where available. The zone classifications and trajectory projections remain useful for identifying trends, even if the absolute thresholds require adjustment.
industry.other.disclaimer: These benchmarks are derived primarily from SaaS company data. Companies in non-SaaS verticals may observe materially different cost structures. Apply professional judgment when interpreting results.
